stem: A patient receiving a blood transfusion develops fever and flank pain after 15 minutes. What is the priority?
option_a: Slow the infusion and recheck temperature
option_b: Administer an antipyretic while blood runs
option_c: Finish the unit then report symptoms
option_d: Stop transfusion, assess the patient, and follow reaction protocol

option_rationales.a: Slowing maintains exposure.
option_rationales.b: Medication does not replace immediate cessation.
option_rationales.c: Continuing potentially incompatible blood is dangerous.
option_rationales.d: Stopping blood and urgent assessment are required.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Slowing maintains exposure. B: Medication does not replace immediate cessation. C: Continuing potentially incompatible blood is dangerous. D: Stopping blood and urgent assessment are required.

stem: A patient has a potassium value of 3.0 mEq/L and is receiving a loop diuretic. Which finding warrants immediate follow-up?
option_a: A new irregular pulse
option_b: Mild dry mouth
option_c: A request for lunch
option_d: Occasional fatigue after walking

option_rationales.a: Hypokalemia can precipitate dysrhythmias.
option_rationales.c: Food requests do not indicate electrical instability.
option_rationales.d: Mild exertional tiredness is nonspecific.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Hypokalemia can precipitate dysrhythmias. B: Dry mouth is less urgent. C: Food requests do not indicate electrical instability. D: Mild exertional tiredness is nonspecific.

stem: A patient 12 hours after hip surgery has oxygen saturation 90%, new chest discomfort, and heart rate 122/min. What is best?
option_a: Provide a routine snack
option_b: Assess breathing and circulation immediately and escalate possible cardiopulmonary complication
option_c: Ask the patient to walk farther
option_d: Wait for morning rounds

option_rationales.a: Nutrition is not first during acute deterioration.
option_rationales.b: New hypoxemia and tachycardia after surgery need urgent assessment.
option_rationales.c: Walking may worsen instability.
option_rationales.d: Delay may miss thromboembolism or other emergencies.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Nutrition is not first during acute deterioration. B: New hypoxemia and tachycardia after surgery need urgent assessment. C: Walking may worsen instability. D: Delay may miss thromboembolism or other emergencies.

stem: A patient receiving tube feeding has the head of the bed at 10 degrees and repeatedly coughs during feeding. Which action is safest?
option_a: Continue feeding because coughing is expected
option_b: Increase feed rate to shorten exposure
option_c: Pause feeding, assess for aspiration and improve positioning as clinically appropriate
option_d: Give oral water to clear the throat

option_rationales.a: Cough can be an aspiration warning.
option_rationales.c: Pausing feed and assessing airway are priorities.
option_rationales.d: Oral water may further increase aspiration risk.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Cough can be an aspiration warning. B: Faster feeding may worsen risk. C: Pausing feed and assessing airway are priorities. D: Oral water may further increase aspiration risk.

stem: An immobile patient reports heel pain but the skin is intact. Which intervention is most appropriate?
option_a: Keep pressure on the heel to prevent movement
option_b: Massage the heel vigorously
option_c: Place a donut ring under the heel
option_d: Use a heel-offloading device and assess the skin regularly

option_rationales.a: Persistent loading can produce pressure injury.
option_rationales.c: Donut designs can concentrate pressure.
option_rationales.d: Offloading and skin checks reduce risk.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Persistent loading can produce pressure injury. B: Massage may injure fragile tissue. C: Donut designs can concentrate pressure. D: Offloading and skin checks reduce risk.

stem: A patient reports dry mouth while NPO awaiting surgery. Which intervention can the nurse provide without violating NPO orders?
option_a: Provide appropriate frequent oral care and approved moistening measures
option_b: Offer a full cup of water
option_c: Give ice chips regardless of the order
option_d: Provide a piece of candy without checking

option_rationales.a: Oral care improves comfort without routine swallowing.
option_rationales.c: Ice chips require specific authorization.
option_rationales.d: Candy could increase aspiration and NPO risk.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Oral care improves comfort without routine swallowing. B: Water may violate NPO orders. C: Ice chips require specific authorization. D: Candy could increase aspiration and NPO risk.

stem: A patient with limited mobility has difficulty reaching the call light. What should the nurse do before leaving?
option_a: Ask the patient to shout for help
option_b: Place the call light and needed items within reach and verify the patient can use it
option_c: Raise all four rails instead
option_d: Tell the patient to wait for scheduled rounds

option_rationales.a: Shouting is unreliable.
option_rationales.b: Reachable assistance supports safety and autonomy.
option_rationales.c: Rails do not replace help access.
option_rationales.d: Waiting can cause unsafe unassisted movement.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Shouting is unreliable. B: Reachable assistance supports safety and autonomy. C: Rails do not replace help access. D: Waiting can cause unsafe unassisted movement.

stem: A patient taking an opioid reports no bowel movement for three days and mild abdominal fullness. What should the RN do?
option_a: Recommend complete bed rest
option_b: Tell the patient it is normal and needs no evaluation
option_c: Assess bowel pattern and implement the ordered constipation prevention or treatment plan
option_d: Give an unprescribed enema

option_rationales.a: Immobility worsens constipation.
option_rationales.c: Assessment and authorized treatment address the cause.
option_rationales.d: Rectal interventions require assessment and appropriate orders.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Immobility worsens constipation. B: Opioid-related constipation requires proactive care. C: Assessment and authorized treatment address the cause. D: Rectal interventions require assessment and appropriate orders.

stem: A patient with a new home blood-pressure cuff asks how to improve reading accuracy. What is best?
option_a: Measure immediately after smoking
option_b: Cross legs and hold the cuff over clothing
option_c: Talk during cuff inflation
option_d: Sit quietly with feet supported and arm at heart level before measurement

option_rationales.a: Nicotine transiently elevates readings.
option_rationales.b: Crossed legs and clothing can alter measurements.
option_rationales.c: Talking affects accuracy.
option_rationales.d: Standard positioning and rest support accurate monitoring.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Nicotine transiently elevates readings. B: Crossed legs and clothing can alter measurements. C: Talking affects accuracy. D: Standard positioning and rest support accurate monitoring.

stem: A patient with diabetes says they often skip breakfast but take the usual rapid-acting insulin dose. What teaching is most important?
option_a: Match mealtime insulin timing to actual meals and discuss skipped-meal instructions with the clinician
option_b: Continue regardless of food
option_c: Double lunchtime insulin to compensate
option_d: Avoid checking glucose on days without breakfast

option_rationales.a: Rapid-acting insulin without food can cause hypoglycemia.
option_rationales.c: Double doses risk low glucose.
option_rationales.d: Monitoring is especially important during schedule changes.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Rapid-acting insulin without food can cause hypoglycemia. B: Unmatched dosing is unsafe. C: Double doses risk low glucose. D: Monitoring is especially important during schedule changes.

stem: A parent asks what to do if an infant develops fever and fewer wet diapers. What is best?
option_a: Restrict feeds for 24 hours
option_b: Seek timely medical advice, especially for young infants, and monitor hydration
option_c: Give aspirin
option_d: Wait until the infant is unable to wake up

option_rationales.a: Reduced intake can worsen dehydration.
option_rationales.b: Fever and reduced output warrant age-sensitive evaluation.
option_rationales.c: Aspirin is not appropriate routine pediatric fever care.
option_rationales.d: Waiting for severe lethargy is dangerous.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Reduced intake can worsen dehydration. B: Fever and reduced output warrant age-sensitive evaluation. C: Aspirin is not appropriate routine pediatric fever care. D: Waiting for severe lethargy is dangerous.

stem: A patient trying to quit smoking says, 'I slipped and had a cigarette yesterday.' Which response best supports continued cessation?
option_a: Say the attempt has failed
option_b: Tell the patient to hide future lapses
option_c: Explore what triggered the lapse and renew a realistic quit plan
option_d: Recommend smoking only during stressful events

option_rationales.a: One lapse need not end the quit attempt.
option_rationales.c: Nonjudgmental problem-solving supports ongoing cessation.
option_rationales.d: Situational smoking sustains exposure.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: One lapse need not end the quit attempt. B: Secrecy prevents support. C: Nonjudgmental problem-solving supports ongoing cessation. D: Situational smoking sustains exposure.

stem: A patient is discharged with a new oral antibiotic. Which teaching best supports safe use?
option_a: Stop as soon as symptoms improve
option_b: Share any remaining pills
option_c: Save unused doses for a future infection
option_d: Follow the prescribed course and call about serious side effects or inability to take doses

option_rationales.a: Early unsupervised discontinuation can compromise treatment.
option_rationales.c: Future illness needs its own evaluation.
option_rationales.d: Clear adherence and adverse-effect instructions support safe use.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Early unsupervised discontinuation can compromise treatment. B: Sharing antibiotics is unsafe. C: Future illness needs its own evaluation. D: Clear adherence and adverse-effect instructions support safe use.

stem: A patient awaiting cancer test results says, 'I'm scared I won't see my children grow up.' Which response is most therapeutic?
option_a: Tell me what concerns you most right now
option_b: There is no reason to worry yet
option_c: At least your children are healthy
option_d: You should try to think positively

option_rationales.a: Open-ended reflection invites expression.
option_rationales.c: Comparisons avoid the concern.
option_rationales.d: Forced positivity can shut down conversation.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Open-ended reflection invites expression. B: False reassurance minimizes fear. C: Comparisons avoid the concern. D: Forced positivity can shut down conversation.

stem: A patient admitted after a panic episode asks whether they are having a heart attack. What should the nurse do first?
option_a: Say that panic attacks cannot affect the body
option_b: Assess symptoms and vital signs to exclude acute medical causes while providing calm support
option_c: Give a paper bag for rebreathing
option_d: Leave the patient alone until symptoms pass

option_rationales.a: Psychiatric symptoms do not exclude medical emergencies.
option_rationales.b: Assessment plus reassurance is safe and therapeutic.
option_rationales.c: Paper-bag rebreathing may cause harm in hypoxemia.
option_rationales.d: Abandonment can worsen distress.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Psychiatric symptoms do not exclude medical emergencies. B: Assessment plus reassurance is safe and therapeutic. C: Paper-bag rebreathing may cause harm in hypoxemia. D: Abandonment can worsen distress.

stem: A patient diagnosed with major depression says, 'My family would be better off if I were dead.' What is the priority nursing response?
option_a: Change the subject to family support
option_b: Assure the patient that they are loved
option_c: Directly assess suicide thoughts, intent, plan and immediate safety
option_d: Ask the patient to keep the thoughts to themselves

option_rationales.a: Avoidance misses risk.
option_rationales.c: Direct evaluation guides level of protection.
option_rationales.d: Secrecy increases danger.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Avoidance misses risk. B: Reassurance cannot replace assessment. C: Direct evaluation guides level of protection. D: Secrecy increases danger.

stem: A patient who recently lost a spouse cries while talking with the nurse. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Explain that crying should stop soon
option_b: Redirect to medication teaching immediately
option_c: Tell the patient other people have worse losses
option_d: Remain present and allow silence, inviting the patient to continue if desired

option_rationales.a: Grief has no fixed timeline.
option_rationales.b: Immediate redirection may interrupt emotional processing.
option_rationales.c: Comparisons invalidate experience.
option_rationales.d: Presence and open invitation support mourning.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Grief has no fixed timeline. B: Immediate redirection may interrupt emotional processing. C: Comparisons invalidate experience. D: Presence and open invitation support mourning.

stem: A patient with kidney disease has potassium 6.4 mEq/L and new peaked T waves. Which action is priority?
option_a: Place on cardiac monitoring and urgently report ECG changes, preparing prescribed treatment
option_b: Encourage potassium-rich juice
option_c: Wait for the next routine metabolic panel
option_d: Give an oral multivitamin

option_rationales.a: Hyperkalemia with ECG effects can cause lethal dysrhythmias.
option_rationales.c: Time-sensitive intervention is needed.
option_rationales.d: Vitamins are unrelated to emergent stabilization.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Hyperkalemia with ECG effects can cause lethal dysrhythmias. B: Extra potassium worsens hyperkalemia. C: Time-sensitive intervention is needed. D: Vitamins are unrelated to emergent stabilization.

stem: A patient with COPD is increasingly breathless, sitting forward and speaking two words at a time. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Ask the patient to walk to loosen secretions
option_b: Assess breathing immediately, support prescribed oxygenation, and escalate care
option_c: Offer a large meal
option_d: Delay for scheduled therapy rounds

option_rationales.a: Exertion worsens distress.
option_rationales.b: Limited speech suggests increased work of breathing requiring urgent assessment.
option_rationales.c: Eating is not first during severe distress.
option_rationales.d: Delay risks fatigue and failure.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Exertion worsens distress. B: Limited speech suggests increased work of breathing requiring urgent assessment. C: Eating is not first during severe distress. D: Delay risks fatigue and failure.

stem: A patient has persistent vomiting, dry mucous membranes, heart rate 120/min and new dizziness on standing. What should be prioritized?
option_a: Encourage unassisted walking
option_b: Restrict all fluids
option_c: Assess volume status and initiate ordered rehydration while monitoring orthostatic safety
option_d: Give a stimulant laxative

option_rationales.a: Falls are likely with orthostasis.
option_rationales.c: Signs suggest hypovolemia and require evaluation and rehydration.
option_rationales.d: Laxatives increase fluid losses.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Falls are likely with orthostasis. B: Restriction worsens depletion. C: Signs suggest hypovolemia and require evaluation and rehydration. D: Laxatives increase fluid losses.

stem: A patient with type 1 diabetes has glucose 320 mg/dL, nausea, abdominal pain and fruity breath. Which nursing action is best?
option_a: Give routine scheduled meal and reassess tomorrow
option_b: Assume simple hyperglycemia without evaluation
option_c: Encourage vigorous exercise
option_d: Check ketones and assess for ketoacidosis, notifying the team promptly

option_rationales.a: Eating without assessment may not be appropriate.
option_rationales.c: Exercise can worsen ketosis in insulin deficiency.
option_rationales.d: Prompt assessment supports treatment of possible DKA.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Eating without assessment may not be appropriate. B: Symptoms suggest possible metabolic acidosis. C: Exercise can worsen ketosis in insulin deficiency. D: Prompt assessment supports treatment of possible DKA.

stem: A patient with heart failure has gained 2.5 kg in three days and now needs more pillows to sleep comfortably. What should the RN do?
option_a: Assess fluid status and respiratory findings and report possible worsening congestion
option_b: Reassure that weight changes never matter
option_c: Recommend drinking extra fluids without an order
option_d: Delay until the annual follow-up

option_rationales.a: Rapid gain and orthopnea suggest fluid retention.
option_rationales.c: Extra fluids may worsen overload.
option_rationales.d: Prompt evaluation may prevent deterioration.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Rapid gain and orthopnea suggest fluid retention. B: Dismissal may miss decompensation. C: Extra fluids may worsen overload. D: Prompt evaluation may prevent deterioration.

stem: A patient develops sudden severe abdominal pain, rigid abdomen, fever and dizziness. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Provide a regular meal
option_b: Keep NPO, assess circulation and escalate possible acute abdominal emergency
option_c: Apply a heating pad and wait
option_d: Give a laxative immediately

option_rationales.a: Oral intake may be unsafe if surgery is needed.
option_rationales.b: Peritoneal signs with systemic symptoms need urgent assessment.
option_rationales.c: Heat may delay appropriate care.
option_rationales.d: Laxatives may worsen a surgical abdomen.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Oral intake may be unsafe if surgery is needed. B: Peritoneal signs with systemic symptoms need urgent assessment. C: Heat may delay appropriate care. D: Laxatives may worsen a surgical abdomen.

stem: A patient recovering from a stroke develops coughing, wet voice, and oxygen desaturation during lunch. Which action is priority?
option_a: Offer thicker liquids without assessment
option_b: Continue feeding more slowly
option_c: Stop oral intake, assess airway and notify the team for swallowing reassessment
option_d: Have the patient lie flat to rest

option_rationales.a: Changing consistency without assessment may remain unsafe.
option_rationales.c: New swallowing changes with desaturation require immediate protection and evaluation.
option_rationales.d: Lying flat increases aspiration risk.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Changing consistency without assessment may remain unsafe. B: Continuing intake risks aspiration. C: New swallowing changes with desaturation require immediate protection and evaluation. D: Lying flat increases aspiration risk.
